Without it the answer's move from 'practising in Colombo' to 'may not attest in Negombo' rests on nothing in the map. Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (8). The gold answer has Ananda signing 'with two witnesses', but no provision in the map fixed the number of witnesses. Rule (8) does. Added as supporting for M027-Q01 and cited by CL-M027-Q01-001.

Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(b). The map cited only s.2(1)(a). Paragraph (b) is a cumulative condition of validity - every executant must affix a thumb impression above or beside the signature on the original, duplicate and protocol, in the presence of the notary and the witnesses - and the question asks how the agreement is to be signed. Added as supporting for M027-Q01 and cited by CL-M027-Q01-001.

question_decisions.note: Both limbs are answerable from the corpus. Kept as proposed gold: the two-notary route (s.31 rule (25) with s.32(2)) and the power-of-attorney route are both grounded in verbatim text, and the registration chain checks out. Two application claims were downgraded to disputed because they turn on facts the matter does not state (Kanthi's judicial zone, and the district in which she resides as opposed to practises). Three provisions were added and one indispensable provision (PROV-M027-015) is partially verified on a temporal point that does not change the outcome.

Sections 27(2), 30, 35(1) and 21(2) were each read in full and each says what the map claims. The answer is correctly confined to Kanthi's own liability and does not assert that the lease is void; the effect on the instrument is raised for the lawyer rather than answered.

Block confirmed independently. Section 3(1) of Act No. 12 of 2006 fixes the rate by Ministerial Order and no Order is in the corpus; a grep over the Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982 returns only ss.19, 24 and 46 on leases and no rate schedule, and the corpus holds no schedule sections for either Act. The chargeability and incidence limbs (s.4(i), s.6(c)) are verified, so the question is answerable except for the figure.

disagreements.researcher_position: Kanthi practises in Colombo and Shantha is in Negombo, so rule (22) prevents her attesting his signature there; the sixty-day limb of rule (30A) therefore applies and rule (29) requires a certified copy to the Negombo Registrar of Lands.
disagreements.verifier_position: The corpus holds no list of judicial zones or land registry divisions, so nothing in it establishes that Negombo is outside the area in Kanthi's warrant. Section 4A makes a warrant for a judicial division extend to the whole judicial zone in which the notary resides, which widens the area rather than narrows it. Rules (26) and (29) also turn on the district in which the notary resides, and the matter says only where she practises. The two-notary and power-of-attorney routes are right either way, so the conclusion survives, but CL-M027-Q01-010 and CL-M027-Q01-012 are marked disputed.
supporting_sources: corpus acts listing (no judicial zone or land registry division source)

disagreements.researcher_position: The printed rule number for PROV-M027-007 is not recoverable from the corpus, and PROV-M027-022 is rule (7)(a).
disagreements.verifier_position: Both numbers are recoverable from the corpus provision ids for section 31: sub-15A/sub-1/par-c and sub-7A/par-a. Section 32(1) corroborates, because it identifies rule (16) as the boundaries rule, which rules out reading the thumb-impression block as rule (16). PROV-M027-007 is rule (15A)(c) and PROV-M027-022 is rule (7A)(a). The second correction has a consequence: section 34(1)(b) fixes a penalty for breach of rule (7) and not rule (7A), so a breach of the notary's stamp duty payment obligation falls under the residual s.34(1)(c).

disagreements.researcher_position: PROV-M027-015 (Registration of Documents Ordinance s.8(b)) is unamended 1927 text, in force at October 2024.
disagreements.verifier_position: The corpus edition of the Ordinance is the 1990 consolidation. The corpus separately holds Registration of Documents (Amendment) Acts No. 48 of 2011, No. 21 of 2013, No. 32 of 2022 and No. 18 of 2024, none of which is folded into that edition. Act No. 18 of 2024 s.2 amends s.8 and s.3 repeals Chapter IV; Act No. 48 of 2011 substitutes s.13(1), whose text the corpus still carries in its pre-2011 form. None of this changes the lease analysis, and Act No. 18 of 2024 commences on a date to be appointed, but the map should not describe these sections as unamended.

CL-M027-Q01-012: asserts that the sixty-day limb of rule (30A) applies and that rule (29) is engaged. Both turn on the district in which Kanthi resides, which the matter does not state, and on Negombo being outside the jurisdiction in which she practises. Marked disputed and lowered to inferential.

temporal_issues: PROV-M027-015: section 8 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance was amended by Act No. 18 of 2024 s.2; the corpus 1990 consolidation predates it. Temporal note corrected. The new subparagraph (xii) excludes agreements under the Secured Transactions law and does not reach a lease.

The 2024 amendments relied on elsewhere (Notaries No. 6 of 2024, Prevention of Frauds No. 4 of 2024, Powers of Attorney No. 3 of 2024) carry no commencement date in the corpus. The researcher assumed they were in force by October 2024 and flagged it; the assumption is not verifiable here and is carried forward. It is low risk on these provisions: the 2024 changes recorded against s.31 sit in the amendment event list, not in the rules relied on, and Act No. 3 of 2024 touches only the definition paragraph (b) (powers executed abroad), s.3D, s.4(1)(b) and Schedule II, none of which the map relies on.

PROV-M027-019 and PROV-M027-025 state fine levels attributed to the Increase of Fines Act No. 12 of 2005. The corpus does record 12-2005 as an amending instrument for the Notaries Ordinance and the figures in ss.30 and 37 are verbatim, so the attribution is consistent, but the corpus does not tie the specific figures to that Act.

case_law_dependence: No case citation appears in any gold answer; the validator's case-law regex is clean.

M027-Q02 comes closest. Whether a deed attested by an uncertificated notary is valid cannot be settled from the corpus - s.33 saves only failures of form under a s.31 rule, and s.30 is not a s.31 rule. The map does not answer that point and confines itself to Kanthi's liability, which is what the question asks, so the question stays statute_only. If a lawyer reads 'liabilities' as including civil liability to the parties for a bad instrument, the question would have to be reserved.

lawyer_questions: Is Negombo outside the area in Kanthi's warrant? The whole of the M027-Q01 answer's premise that she cannot travel and attest there rests on this, and the corpus has no list of judicial zones. A lawyer should confirm the zone allocation and, separately, whether the examiner intended the answer to turn on it at all or simply on Shantha's inability to travel.

Does 'liabilities' in Q4(2)(b) extend to the fate of the lease itself? If the expected answer includes whether a deed attested without the yearly certificate is valid, that needs authority outside the statutory corpus and M027-Q02 should be reserved rather than proposed gold.

Rule (7A)(a) puts payment of stamp duty on the notary while s.6(c) of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act puts it on the lessee. The map treats these as compatible (incidence versus mechanics). Should the gold answer say so expressly, and which penalty limb of s.34 applies to a breach of rule (7A)?

For Q4(2)(c), should the benchmark carry the Gazette Order fixing lease stamp duty as of October 2024, or should the question stay blocked? It is the only thing standing between the map and a complete answer.
